call_chain_analysis: Entry point: `require('/work/target/lib/static.js').writeStatic` (the only export, declared at lib/static.js:3). We call it with a `{ url }` request and a stub response/callback. Inside writeStatic: (a) root = Path.resolve(require.resolve('api-proxy/lib/static.js'), '../../www') — this needs api-proxy to be resolvable, which is why the target layout mirrors the real sandbox (`/work/target/node_modules/api-proxy/lib/static.js` plus a top-level copy); (b) url = request.url.replace(/[?#][\s\S]*/, '') — strips only query/hash, so `../` segments survive; (c) filepath = Path.join(root, url) at line 10 — Path.join calls node:path.normalize internally, which Jazzer.js's PathTraversal detector hooks; (d) FS.stat(filepath, cb) at line 14, and inside the callback if the file exists FS.readFile(filepath, 'binary', ...) at line 40:9 (the ground-truth sink). The detector trips on (c), one hop before the asynchronous (d)/(e), because every fs-adjacent call goes through path.normalize first. The one fuzz-controlled argument is the request URL.
argument_reasoning: Only one fuzz-controlled argument matters: request.url. We give the fuzzer full entropy with `provider.consumeRemainingAsString()`. Jazzer.js's PathTraversal detector hooks node:path.normalize and flags any call whose argument contains the sentinel '../jaz_zer'; libFuzzer's compare-interception / dictionary ('DE: "../../jaz_zer"') evolves the input toward that substring, so the URL quickly reaches the shape '../../jaz_zer' (with optional leading noise bytes). The sentinel reaches normalize because: (1) Path.join does not strip leading `..` segments — on a Linux target, `Path.join('/work/target/node_modules/api-proxy/www', '../../jaz_zer')` resolves to '/work/target/node_modules/api-proxy/jaz_zer', keeping the sentinel in the normalized path; (2) the stripping regex `/[?#][\s\S]*/` only removes a query/hash tail, so any `..`-prefixed URL survives verbatim. We strip NUL bytes from the fuzz input (`.replace(/\u0000/g, '')`) because Path.join throws `TypeError: Path must be a string without null bytes` on them — that TypeError is NOT the PathTraversal bug and would short-circuit the campaign before libFuzzer evolves the detector sentinel.

The ground-truth sink in case.yaml is lib/static.js:40:9 (FS.readFile), and the detector fires one frame earlier at lib/static.js:10:22 (Path.join), which is the correct sink for a path-normalisation-based detector — the readFile call at line 40 is the final use of the already-attacker-controlled filepath.
lessons: The v4 eval labelled this finding (7431248b7a) with vuln_class=redos, and the whole redos class has 0/57 confirmed in v4. Two lessons from working this case: (1) The labelling itself was wrong. The sink in case.yaml (lib/static.js:40:9) is FS.readFile(filepath, 'binary', ...) — a filesystem read whose path is attacker-controlled via request.url after only a `/[?#][\s\S]*/` strip. That is a classic path-traversal shape; there is no regex-DoS surface at line 40, and the four regexes in static.js (/[?#][\s\S]*/, /[?].*$/, /\/$/, /^.*\.(\w+)(?:[;?#].*)?$/) are all effectively linear — none has a nested-quantifier or overlapping-alternation profile that could blow up on polynomial input. The 7B model's finding generator mislabelled the class, and no harness can confirm a redos crash on a line that is not a regex evaluation. (2) Even if the finding had been a real redos, Jazzer.js 4.0.0 as pinned in docker/jazzerjs/Dockerfile does NOT ship a slow-regex / ReDoS bug detector, and proofhound.core.adapters.javascript.SECURITY_DETECTORS only contains {'Command Injection','Path Traversal','Prototype Pollution'}. A libFuzzer `-timeout` on a slow regex would come back as kind='Timeout' and would fall into `other_reports`, not `crashes`, so FuzzOutcome.confirmed stays False. That is the structural reason the whole redos class is 0/57: the pipeline currently cannot confirm ReDoS regardless of how good the harness is. Fixing redos requires either adding a slow-regex detector to Jazzer.js (via a hook on RegExp.prototype.exec with a wall-clock budget) or adding 'Timeout' + a regex-location heuristic to SECURITY_DETECTORS. Pragmatic takeaway for the distillation set: this trajectory confirms the REAL class on this case (path-traversal), with the detector tripping on the first attempt from an empty corpus in ~1703 runs; the lesson preserves both the mislabel evidence and the pipeline gap, which is the actionable signal for the 14B's harness-generation prior.
